facts.statement: The genus Erquitaia was first described by the scientist Henri Cappetta in 1989.
facts.quote: Erquitaia was originally described by Henri Cappetta in 1989.

facts.statement: Erquitaia is a little-known genus of prehistoric sharks belonging to the galeomorph group.
facts.quote: Erquitaia is a poorly known genus of prehistoric galeomorph shark

facts.statement: Fossils of Erquitaia are found in rocks that date to the Maastrichtian stage.
facts.quote: whose fossils are found in rocks dating from the Maastrichtian stage.

facts.statement: Researchers initially misidentified Erquitaia as a ray and classified it in the order Rajiformes.
facts.quote: It was thought to be a ray and was placed in the order Rajiformes.

facts.statement: Erquitaia belongs to the shark superorder Galeomorphi, a group containing all modern sharks except dogfish and their relatives.
facts.quote: into the shark super order Galeomorphi, which includes all modern sharks except the dogfish and their relatives.

facts.statement: The parent group for the genus Erquitaia is Galeomorphi.
Erquitaia is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
